creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Today a daemon restart returns the pane tree but "the scrollback is gone". `docs/architecture.md` says "Persist intent, never observation", and terminals carry secrets, so persisting scrollback reverses a stated doctrine and writes those secrets to disk. That is the owner's call.

If yes, write `terminal.replay()` to disk rather than a libghostty snapshot. It works today, any later libghostty reads it back, and it already has an oracle.

Snapshots (snapshot.h) carry more: the saved cursor, the kitty keyboard stack, images. But the header excludes the byte format from the ABI promise, and snapshot/main.zig calls version 1 "the work-in-progress format that we intended to continue to break". #13566 broke it at version 1, and testdata/complete-v1.hex changed between the pin and vt-1.0.0 with the version still 1. Readers check only the version number, so an old file could decode into a subtly wrong grid. Any file would need stamping with the exact pin and patch hash and discarding on mismatch, so every re-pin would lose saved scrollback.

Either format has no incremental encode: each save is a whole pane under its lock, and a crash loses everything since the last one.
title: Should a pane's scrollback survive a daemon restart?
